messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High KV cache memory growth observed on prod-cluster-3. Latency SLO breaches for embeddings route. Auto-pager triggered for oncall rotation.

marta (oncall): seeing 5xx spikes and tail latency up ~3x. KV cache resident size jumped from 18GB -> 72GB in ~12m on several workers. Noticed continuous-batching traffic surge (~200k requests/min) to 3 models.

kevin (eng-runtime): thanks. Any recent rollouts to batching or cache code?

marta (oncall): no code deploys in last 2h. We did push a config change to default batch window earlier today (ops change).

jay (sre): attaching quick heap map from node-13: lots of fragmented GPU allocations, many small KV slabs. Looks like arena fragmentation + repeated small-prefetch KV writes.

kevin (eng-runtime): hmm. That fragmentation profile looks like recent change to KV write path that allowed aggressive async prefetch. Could be continuous batching causing tiny partial KV fills.

eli (platform): customers impacted: 3 mid-market tenants on dedicated pools reporting timeouts; alerting shows elevated error rate for embeddings and chat. ETA SLA impacted.

marta (oncall): immediate ask: mitigate customer impact, stop blowup, restore SLOs. Proposed temp mitigations: 1) throttle continuous batching window; 2) force KV compaction on affected nodes; 3) restart a small subset if compaction not reclaiming.

kevin (eng-runtime): agree. Quick mitigation steps we can run non-disruptively: set env `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128` on runtime binary (works for pytorch allocator tuning), and reduce continuous-batcher config: `max_contiguous_batch_tokens` -> 64, `min_batch_delay_ms` -> 15. That should reduce small-slab churn.

marta (oncall): running throttle change now to canary group (10% workers) via console. Command: `/deploy-config continuous_batcher.production --set max_contiguous_batch_tokens=64 --canary 10%`

ops-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: continuous_batcher.production updated (canary 10%) by marta.

jay (sre): starting compaction on node-13 and node-17: `curl -XPOST http://node-13.internal/_kv/compaction` -> returned 202.

kevin (eng-runtime): while compaction runs, let's also apply `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` change via runtime flags on the canary pods. Command snippet for k8s patch:

```
kubectl -n runtime patch deployment runtime-worker --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"worker","env":[{"name":"PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF","value":"max_split_size_mb:128"}]}]}}}}'
```

marta (oncall): canary config rolled. Monitoring. Latency down ~15% on canary nodes but global still high.

eli (platform): customer impact update: two tenants still seeing >10% 5xx window. We're routing more of their traffic to dedicated fallback model variant (lower memory) while we stabilize.

jay (sre): compaction finished on the two nodes, memory reclaimed ~9GB each. However fragmentation persisted on others. Paging shows allocator hitting many CUDA sbrk-like ops.

kevin (eng-runtime): ok next step: globally apply the batch throttle for 15 minutes to flatten churn while we craft a targeted patch. I'll open a hotfix PR to make continuous-batching respect a `min_batch_fill_ratio` so we avoid tiny partial KVs.

marta (oncall): global throttle applied: `max_contiguous_batch_tokens=64` for all runtime workers. Ops-bot: note.

ops-bot: CONFIG-CHANGE: continuous_batcher.production updated (global) by marta.

marta (oncall): tail latency improved to near-SLO after global throttle + compaction, errors down to baseline for affected tenants. Continuing to monitor for 30m.

kevin (eng-runtime): PR opened: `runtime#4821` includes: - enforce min_batch_fill_ratio=0.6 - conservative prefetch batching - optional per-model max_kv_write_size. Requesting expedited review.

eli (platform): create incident ticket and notify account teams for the two tenants. I'll draft a customer-impact blurb: short outage window, mitigation steps, next steps.

marta (oncall): two follow-ups before handoff: 1) confirm PR gate and rollout plan (canary -> 25% -> 100%), 2) schedule a postmortem to look at the config change that enabled aggressive batching earlier today.

jay (sre): adding forensic notes: collect `nvprof`/allocator traces from 6 impacted nodes for correlation with request traces. Save `/var/log/runtime/kv-alloc-{node}.log` to S3 path `s3://redwood-incident-logs/2498761234/`

marta (oncall): handoff summary for night shift (please paste into your handoff): "KV cache fragmentation caused by continuous-batching partial writes after a config change. Immediate mitigation: global throttle and targeted compaction reclaimed memory and restored SLOs. Hotfix PR opened to stop tiny-batch writes. Owners: kevin -> runtime fix; jay -> compaction/forensics; eli -> customer comms. Monitor for 4h; if memory regresses by >20% from current baseline, escalate back to oncall."

kevin (eng-runtime): adding owner tag to PR and starting canary deployment in 10m once QA signoff is done.

eli (platform): customer comms sent to account teams with ETA for full rollout ~3h.

marta (oncall): handing off to night oncall @ 03:00. Please watch `kv-cache-resident` and `embeddings-latency-p95` alerts. I'll be reachable if needed. :wave:

ops-bot: HANDOFF: oncall -> night-oncall by marta at shift change.

jay (sre): logged followup tasks: - run extended compaction sweep job weekly - add telemetry for small-KV-write ratio - add alert for rapid cache-resident % growth.

kevin (eng-runtime): leaving a link to the hotfix PR and rollout playbook: https://git.redwood/runtime/pull/4821 and https://confluence.redwood/internal/kv-frag-playbook

marta (oncall): closing pager for now. Will reopen if we see regression. :thumbsup:
